• Project Title: Tracer FIRE Cybersecurity Incident Response Training
      Sponsor: Sandia National Laboratories
      Problem: Simulated post-breach environment requiring forensic investigation of attacker activity across a compromised SOC network.
      Approach: Used Elastic SIEM for log correlation and Azure Data Explorer (ADX) for structured KQL-based queries to identify indicators of compromise and trace lateral movement. Supplemented with Velociraptor for endpoint forensics and Malcom for network graph analysis.
      Outcome: Completed CTF-style incident response exercise with structured documentation of findings, attacker timelines, and control gap recommendations.
      Relevance: SIEM operations, threat hunting, log analysis, KQL, incident documentation, forensics
      View project →

    • Project Title: Remote PC Power Management using IoT Platform
      Problem: Needed a reliable way to remotely power-cycle a home PC from out of state without expensive KVM-over-IP hardware.
      Approach: Programmed an ESP32 microcontroller in C++ to trigger PC power and reset lines via relay, controlled through the Blynk IoT cloud dashboard. Layered Tailscale for secure remote network access and Parsec for low-latency remote desktop once the machine was online.
      Outcome: Full remote power management operational from the Bay Area while at school in Tempe — cold boots, hard resets, and graceful shutdowns all accessible via phone.
      Relevance: Embedded systems, C++, IoT platforms, remote access, network security


    • Project Title: AI-Powered Vision Assistance Prototype
      Problem: Visually impaired users lack affordable, real-time assistive devices that can identify hazards and provide immediate audio feedback.
      Approach: Built a wearable prototype using Raspberry Pi with camera module, ultrasonic sensors, and a speaker. Integrated the Gemini API for vision inference and wrote processing logic in Python. Used GitHub Copilot throughout to maintain code quality during a tight academic sprint.
      Outcome: Functional prototype achieving 25ms response time and 99% accuracy in controlled testing. Presented to course evaluators as a complete hardware-software system.
      Relevance: Embedded systems, Python, Gemini API, AI-assisted development, hardware integration, testing
      View project →

    • Project Title: GPU Thermal Optimization
      Problem: High-end GPU running at unsafe temperatures under load, causing thermal throttling and system instability.
      Approach: Ran stress benchmarks and monitored thermals to confirm GPU overheating as root cause. Disassembled the card, cleaned old thermal pads and paste, applied fresh Thermal Grizzly materials, and validated recovery with a repeat benchmark.
      Outcome: Temperatures reduced to safe operating range. System stable under sustained load with documented before/after thermal profiles.
      Relevance: Hardware diagnostics, reliability engineering, preventive maintenance, benchmarking
      View project →

    • Project Title: Cloud Email and Workspace Migration
      Sponsor: Volunteer Project
      Problem: Scout organization running a legacy email platform that was unreliable, costly, and not manageable by non-technical volunteers.
      Approach: Planned and executed a staged migration to Google Workspace with zero downtime, including DNS cutover, mailbox migration, and youth protection compliance validation. Produced runbooks and trained an adult leader for ongoing administration.
      Outcome: 50+ users migrated successfully with no service interruption. Eliminated $200/year in fees and left the organization with a maintainable, documented system.
      Relevance: Change management, Google Workspace, DNS, IT documentation, stakeholder communication


    • Project Title: Home Network Infrastructure Upgrade
      Problem: Persistent wireless failures and an unsegmented flat network in a busy household with 60+ devices.
      Approach: Diagnosed root cause (ISP modem bridge mode misconfiguration + channel congestion), then deployed a Ubiquiti UniFi stack with proper VLAN segmentation separating IoT, guest, and internal traffic. Documented topology, access control lists, and configuration baselines.
      Outcome: Network outages reduced from ~50 per year to 1. Clean segmentation improved security posture and gave a documented baseline for future changes.
      Relevance: Network engineering, Ubiquiti/UniFi, VLANs, documentation, troubleshooting
      View project →
